title: [Bug]: Scheduler permanently stops admitting requests once running + skipped_waiting ("deferred") reaches max_num_seqs - engine reports healthy, KV cache mostly free, only a restart recovers

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Environment (summary) - vLLM v0.27.1, OpenAI-compatible server (Docker), single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell - Image: official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1` locally rebuilt with transformers pinned to 5.14.1 (workaround for #51744); vLLM/scheduler code unmodified. Full `collect_env` output in the environment section. - Model: nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4, `--max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` - MTP speculative decoding via separate BF16 drafter (`num_speculative_tokens: 4`) - `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4` - Clients: LiteLLM proxy → `POST /v1/chat/completions` with SSE streaming + tool calls. We do NOT use the session-based streaming-input / realtime API (no `resumable` requests; verified zero realtime/StreamingInput log lines). ## Symptom During a client traffic burst (~16 req/min sustained, many held open 600 s by the proxy and retried), the scheduler wedged permanently: | UTC | Running | Waiting | deferred | KV cache | gen tok/s | |-------|---------|---------|----------|----------|-----------| | 10:08 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.0% | idle | | 10:45 | 29 | 92 | 92 | 90.0% | 53.3 | | 10:57 | 3 | 227 | 227 | 20.9% | 1.2 ← collapse | | 12:10 | 4 | 487 | 468 | 20.0% | 5.5 | At 12:20, over a 60 s `/metrics` window: prompt throughput 1,946 tok/s, generation 0.48 tok/s, ~0.2 engine steps/s, `request_success_total` +0 (all finish reasons), `num_preemptions_total` 0, `abort` count 0 over the container's 4-day lifetime. `num_requests_waiting_by_reason`: `deferred` 473, `capacity` 19. GPU at 100% SM / 11% memory-bus (pure prefill), prefix-cache hit rate degraded 77% → 18%. `/health` returned 200 throughout; Docker healthcheck stayed green. The state never recovered on its own (observed >1.5 h); a container restart fully cleared it. ## Analysis - The collapse point matches `len(running) + blocked == max_num_seqs (256)` exactly (227 deferred + 29 running). After that, the admission gate (`num_running = len(self.running) + self.num_waiting_for_streaming_input; if num_running >= self.max_num_running_reqs: break`) appears to break out on every step even though the KV cache is ~80% free. - `reason="deferred"` maps to `len(self.skipped_waiting)` as a whole (`WAITING_FOR_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_GRAMMAR` | `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` | `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ`), so we cannot tell from metrics which status held the 473. `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` is ruled out (no KV connector configured). We don't use the streaming-input API, which per #28973 is the only path into `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` — yet `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request()` returning `False` unconditionally for that status (unchanged on current `main`) is the same never-promoted pattern PR #45406 describes for `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. The remaining candidate is grammar-waiting requests from the tool-call-heavy traffic never being promoted/cleaned; notably, zero xgrammar/structured_output warnings or errors were logged in the incident window, and no requests finished with `finished_reason="error"`. - Whatever the sub-state: requests parked in `skipped_waiting` were never promoted, never aborted, and (apparently) counted against admission, so the engine served ~0 requests indefinitely while accepting new ones and reporting healthy. ## Related (checked, believed non-duplicate) - #45406 / #45387 / #45388: identical structural pattern (parked requests never promoted → `schedule()` empty forever, restart-only), but for the KV-connector status. Still open/unmerged. - #52693 / #52717: same streaming-input code area, but an acute EngineCore crash, not a silent wedge. - #41967: streaming+tool-call under MTP, but a content-corruption bug (closed). ## Repro Production incident; we do not have a standalone repro. Trigger conditions were: sustained concurrent streaming tool-call load (hundreds of connections held open by an upstream proxy with 600 s timeout + retries) against a single engine at `max-num-seqs 256`. Happy to provide fuller metric dumps or log excerpts on request, but our capacity for interactive debugging is limited — treating this primarily as an incident report with data. `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` and `VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1` were not enabled (production system; the trace overhead is not viable there) — for what it's worth, the standard logs contained zero WARNING/ERROR lines in the entire incident window. If the wedge recurs despite our new admission limits upstream of vLLM, we can attempt a capture with DEBUG logging enabled. We searched existing and past issues before filing; the closest matches and why we believe this is not a duplicate are listed under "Related" below. ## Suggested direction Same as #45406's premise: statuses in `skipped_waiting` need either a promotion path, a cleanup/abort path (e.g., on client disconnect), or exclusion from the admission count — no status should be able to consume scheduler capacity irrevocably. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
